Three exact runs · 3,000,000 total ticks · 440×735 cells · 1 px per cell

Evolution under crowding and local color rarity

A visual and quantitative report on Sampler 24: what evolved, what natural selection appears to reward, how bloom color organizes from neighborhood to world scale, and why the system is promising without yet being open-ended, speciated, or coevolutionary.

Central finding. The three runs reproduce one strong transition—from a straight, one-flower ancestor to ramified multi-terminal genomes—and one strong color result—a nearly complete hue wheel. After roughly 10K ticks, however, programmed complexity plateaus while the world becomes developmentally censored by crowding. The most genuinely surprising result is not unlimited novelty; it is seed-dependent symmetry breaking: one run evolves a predominantly horizontal architecture while the other two remain vertical.

01 · Bottom line

A real evolutionary ecology—inside a narrow adaptive vocabulary

Sampler 24 clearly implements Darwinian evolution: clonal replication, heritable mutation, differential survival and reproduction, local competition for space, and an explicit local rarity advantage for flower hue. It is more than a procedural drawing. But the evidence supports bounded adaptive evolution, not open-ended evolution, speciation, or coevolution.

8/10Evolution

A repeatable macro-transition, thousands of generations, crowding-mediated development and ecological selection.

8/10Color diversity

One ancestral hue becomes 250–254 occupied hue bins and roughly 196–211 effective hues.

2/10Open-endedness

Program size, interaction types and functional roles plateau; novelty does not create new niches.

1/10Speciation / coevolution

No mating barriers, no persistent lineage record, and no distinct partners undergoing reciprocal adaptation.

The honest research claim: this is a compact, unusually auditable spatial eco-evolutionary model with a productive combination of developmental grammar, metabolism, crowding and local negative frequency dependence. Its strongest publishable future lies in controlled experiments on multiscale color structure, developmental censoring, and symmetry breaking—not in claiming a new general theory of evolution.

02 · Visual chronology

All 18 exact frames

Read down the logarithmic time axis. The first transition is population fill; the second is architectural branching; the third is color-wheel expansion. The late frames are not simply “more” of the early frames: they show a plateau, secondary pruning of flower terminals, and run-specific orientation.

Tick 10

No selection result is visible yet: all 40 founders are the same red ancestor.

Tick 100

Small mutations are visible but sparse. The dominant exact form still holds 82–86% of living plants.

Tick 1K

The first ecological carpet forms. Exact-form dominance collapses to roughly 2%, while multibloom branches become the broad majority.

Tick 10K

The decisive morphology transition is complete. Nearly every programmed body has more than one flower terminal, although crowding prevents most terminals from appearing.

Tick 100K

The hue wheel is almost filled. One-bloom branching reappears in all runs, a repeated simplification of terminal investment rather than a return to simple stalks.

Tick 1M

Population, complexity and hue statistics have entered a fluctuating plateau. Seed 2 is horizontally organized; seeds 1 and 3 remain vertically organized.

03 · Morphology

The common body plan changes once, then refines

At 10 ticks every plant is the two-node ancestor. By 1K, branching and duplicate flower terminals are the majority strategy. By 10K, they are nearly universal. From 100K onward, all three runs partially prune terminal flowers while retaining ramified stems.

Why branching wins—what is observed and what is inferred

income = open faces × 0.02

Only tissue earns energy, from all eight exposed faces. There is no shade direction and no reward for height itself.

upkeep = cells × .004 + .60(age/200)²

More tissue costs more, but total exposed area can outweigh cell upkeep until senescence dominates.

seed cost = 7 × (1 − rarity bonus)

Every realized flower is a launch site, yet all heads draw from one energy pool. Extra heads are opportunity, not free fecundity.

Direct result: the multibloom-brancher category rises from 0% at tick 10 to 99.8–99.9% at tick 10K. Mean programmed nodes rise from 2.0 to 17.9. Mean programmed flower terminals peak near 5.4, while only 1.4 blooms are actually built.

Mechanistic inference: branching supplies several growth fronts and several possible bloom sites in a congested world. A blocked job disappears without paying its build cost, so a large genome can act like a portfolio of attempts: the environment selects which subtrees become phenotype. That makes branching robust to local obstruction and makes latent genome bloat unusually cheap.

Cross-sectional evidence: at 1M, realized cell count has a modest positive Spearman association with age in all runs (ρ=0.23, 0.23, 0.26); span behaves similarly. Density is weakly negative. This is consistent with larger, more open bodies surviving longer, but it is not a lifetime reproductive-success estimate.

Survivorship warning. A living snapshot overcounts long-lived plants and misses forms that reproduced rapidly and died. Parent IDs, dead organisms and per-plant lifetime seed counts were not retained. The report therefore calls selection “plausible” where the mechanism and prevalence agree, not proven by a pedigree-level selection gradient.

A visual sequence of the transition

04 · Reproducible extremes

Longest, shortest, widest, largest—and the oddest implementation escape

“Most unique” is not a single objective quantity: more than half of exact forms are singletons at late checkpoints. The defensible substitutes are reproducible extremes in realized geometry and program–body mismatch.

Across the final snapshots: the largest bodies contain 65, 77 and 67 cells; the widest bounding boxes are 21, 34 and 21 cells; the tallest are 30, 23 and 38 cells; and the most flower-rich bodies carry 5, 4 and 4 realized blooms for seeds 1–3 respectively.

The 29-node “breakthrough” is a loophole, not a major evolutionary transition. Graft mutations respect MAX_NODES = 20, but converting a flower instruction into a shoot inserts a fresh terminal flower without rechecking the cap. Between 8% and 14% of final living genomes exceed 20 nodes. Evolution found and occupied a representational escape route, a familiar kind of result in digital evolution.[10] It is scientifically informative about the implementation, but it should be repaired or explicitly redefined before claiming unbounded program growth.
05 · Flower color

Globally broad, locally inherited, and scale-dependent

Color is the cleanest success. The red ancestor diffuses around the circular hue wheel until nearly every of 256 bins is occupied. But the world is not a fine-grained random mixture: short dispersal creates same-hue neighborhoods, while local rarity selection differentiates patches.

The local-to-global law

At 1M, nearest-neighbor plants differ by only 25.4–26.8 hue steps on average. For pairs within eight cells the gap is 25.4–26.4; within 32 cells it is 45.5–49.2; within 128 cells it is 58.2–60.2. Globally it reaches 61.9–62.8, close to the uniform-wheel expectation of 64.

This resolves the apparent contradiction in the images. Short-range inheritance and dispersal create color patches. The explicit rarity discount then rewards a bloom that differs from the circular mean of flowers in the surrounding 3×3 array of 16-cell blocks—roughly a 48×48 neighborhood. Patch boundaries and mixed neighborhoods receive stronger selection for divergence than uniform interiors.

The theoretical maximum seed-cost reduction is 50%, but the realized mean at 1M is only 13.0–14.7%. The rule is effective without usually paying its maximum reward. The distinction matters: the diverse palette is an emergent spatial consequence of an explicit negative-frequency-dependent color rule, not an emergent discovery that color matters.

Do not call this novelty search. Novelty search compares behavioral descriptors against a population and archive while ignoring an objective.[5] Quality-diversity methods retain high-performing exemplars across behavioral niches.[6] Sampler 24 instead gives one hand-selected phenotype coordinate—hue—a direct local reproductive discount, with no archive and no behavior-space illumination.
06 · The three goals

Two meaningful successes; one important shortfall

7/10

Legibility

Achieved locally, compromised globally. Each organism is a one-cell-wide graph with a consistent stem and bloom grammar; the isolated crops are immediately readable. Exact pixels and state make every visual claim auditable. At 100K–1M the full field is close to visual saturation, so individual organisms merge into texture unless enlarged or isolated. Black ground, stem/bloom contrast and nearest-neighbor rendering help, but negative space is scarce.

8/10

Evolution and natural selection

1/10 coevolution

Natural selection is strongly achieved. The common ancestor is replaced by ramified, multi-terminal programs in all three runs, and thousands of generations accumulate under local competition. Coevolution is not demonstrated. Competition and frequency dependence are interactions, but Janzen’s precise criterion requires evolutionary change in one population followed by an evolutionary response in another.[14] There are no distinguishable partner roles, no heritable interaction traits aimed at specific partners and no lineage record with which to establish reciprocity.

7/10

Biophilic / millefleur form

Achieved as a generative aesthetic, especially at neighborhood scale. Cross-shaped blooms, pale articulated stems, repeated small motifs and the black field read as a living stitched carpet. The color-patch crops are particularly successful. The limitation is morphological convergence: many exact genomes produce variations on the same rectilinear brancher, and crowding censors the most elaborate programs. A stronger result would preserve the simplicity while creating several visibly different ecological roles.

Speciation remains unsupported. Under a general lineage concept, species are separately evolving metapopulation lineages.[13] Here reproduction is clonal, there is no gene flow to restrict, and more than half of exact forms are one-off mutations. Spatial or hue clusters can be called patches, morphs, or candidate ecotypes; they cannot yet be defended as species. Seed 2’s horizontal regime is the best proto-ecotype hypothesis, not proof.
07 · Rare and consequential events

What deserves attention—and what does not

Strong repeated breakthroughs

Multi-terminal branching. Rare two-bloom mutants exist by tick 100 in every run, dominate by 1K and nearly fix by 10K. Because it repeats independently, this is the strongest evidence of selection rather than accident.

Full-wheel color expansion. By 100K each run occupies 250–254 hue bins. This is an excellent implementation result, but it is a response to the designed rarity rule, not an unexpected new adaptive dimension.

Secondary terminal pruning. Mean programmed flowers falls from about 5.4 at 10K to 2.8 at 1M, while mean branch points rises from 4.2 to 4.9. All runs retain ramification but reduce terminal investment—a repeated refinement that the images alone conceal.

Run-specific or ambiguous events

Horizontal seed 2. At 1M, 62% of seed-2 bodies are wide, versus 2–4% in seeds 1 and 3. Because income uses eight-face exposure and seed movement is isotropic, there is no obvious direct horizontal fitness term. This makes historical contingency or spontaneous symmetry breaking plausible. Three runs are insufficient to estimate rarity.

Twenty-node escape. Evolution crosses the advertised cap through a mutation-path inconsistency. Valuable bug discovery; not a biological major transition.

Mutation cloud. Late runs contain 1,367–1,451 exact forms, 51–55% of them singletons, while the most common exact form is ~0.5%. This is high standing variation around a narrow family, not evidence of thousands of species.

Most promising follow-up hypothesis: seed 2’s orientation is a macroscopic order parameter produced by local packing and founder history. Run 50–100 seeds, calculate orientation polarization continuously, and test for a bimodal final distribution. If runs reliably choose one of two symmetry-related regimes, that is a clean and potentially publishable result.
08 · Scholarly position

Novel as a compact combination; not novel in its ingredients

In scholarly terms, Sampler 24 is a spatial, individual-based digital evolution model with a recursive developmental grammar, embodied energetic physiology, clonal heredity, local crowding, and explicit negative frequency-dependent selection on a circular phenotype.

Presentation and auditability: medium.

A Tao-like methodological lesson: choose invariants and move between scales

The productive connection is methodological, not ornamental. Circular hue distance is the correct invariant under wraparound; exact form code separates genotype from realized geometry; open-face accounting is the local energetic invariant; and the radius curve links neighborhood structure to global structure. These choices turn an attractive field into falsifiable statements. The next experiment should predeclare a small set of order parameters—orientation polarization, genotype–phenotype realization ratio, lineage diversity, interaction reciprocity—and follow them continuously.

The Ackley test: locality is necessary but not sufficient

Ackley’s robust-first program argues for spatial organization, asynchronous local interaction, continuous self-construction and indefinite scalability without unique global addresses.[11][12] Sampler 24 is aligned in spirit—local bodies, local collisions, local color neighborhoods, damage through death and regrowth—but not in architecture. It uses a finite fixed rectangle, synchronous global ticks, central arrays, a global population loop and a centralized bloom tally. It is a good microscope for local evolutionary ecology, not a robust indefinitely scalable computing substrate.

Value, without flattery

Artistic/generative value: high. It produces coherent living tapestries whose rules remain visible. Educational value: high. Mutation, development, selection and spatial frequency dependence can be inspected directly. Scientific value today: moderate. The system is hypothesis-generating and beautifully auditable, but only three runs, six snapshots and no lineage/event log prevent strong causal claims. Breakthrough status today: no. A publishable contribution would require a precise phenomenon, controls, replication, lineage instrumentation and an analysis plan—not merely a longer run.

Minimum publication-grade package: 50–100 seeds; continuous lineage and birth/death/seed logs; neutral and no-color controls; mutation-rate and world-size sweeps; preregistered orientation and multiscale hue statistics; an ablation that charges for failed developmental jobs; and permutation or matched-lineage tests distinguishing selection from survivorship.
09 · Seven viable redesigns

Add reciprocal adaptive dimensions, not weather bookkeeping

Light, rain and generic soil/litter fields usually impose another external optimization surface. They can be ecologically realistic yet still drive convergence toward one better collector. The proposals below are ranked by their chance of improving the three goals while preserving the system’s visual simplicity.

highest

Partner-specific pollen plus limited recombination

Smallest ruleA flower can seed only after receiving pollen from a nearby bloom. Add one heritable compatibility/preference hue or tag; offspring recombine one or two grammar subtrees.
Natural pressureRare compatible partners, pollen reach, morphology and mate choice jointly determine reproduction—without a global fitness score.
Expected visualAssortative color neighborhoods, hybrid boundary zones, flowering corridors and possibly stable mating clusters.
Why deeperGene flow and its restriction become real. Divergence can create reproductive isolation, making speciation testable rather than metaphorical.
Failure modeOne universal compatibility tag fixes, or mate limitation crashes the world.
Keep / kill testRun 30 seeds to 100K. Keep only if the compatibility matrix becomes modular, cross-cluster mating falls, and ≥2 clusters persist for 500+ generations without being hard-coded.
coevolution

Heritable contact chemistry: exchange, theft or defense

Smallest rulePermit contact at designated tips. Give each contact tip one tag and one response: donate a bounded energy unit, steal it, block it, or ignore. Conserve energy exactly.
Natural pressureFitness depends on the traits of encountered neighbors. A successful exploit changes selection on defenses and partner choice.
Expected visualHighlighted contact seams, defensive spacing, mutualistic lattices, parasites tracing hosts and red-queen patch dynamics.
Why deeperThis supplies the missing reciprocal adaptive loop and allows organisms to create niches for other organisms.
Failure modeUniversal avoidance wins; theft becomes a trivial dominant strategy; contacts become unreadable clutter.
Keep / kill testTrack tag-response frequencies, directed energy flow and lagged cross-correlations. Keep only if one lineage’s change predicts a compensating change in another and ablation of either partner reduces the other.
easy win

Evolvable seed dispersal with an explicit fecundity trade-off

Smallest ruleEncode walk length or kernel width. Make each seed’s energy cost increase monotonically with expected distance.
Natural pressureShort dispersers keep local kin patches and produce more seeds; long dispersers reach empty sites and escape competition.
Expected visualColonizer fronts, compact competitor patches, dispersal clines and sharper local ecotypes.
Why deeperIt adds a spatial life-history axis that couples directly to crowding and color patch scale. Competition–dispersal trade-offs are theoretically capable of structuring diversity.[16]
Failure modeAn intermediate distance fixes everywhere; periodic boundaries or edge effects manufacture a false optimum.
Keep / kill testRun tiled and bounded worlds. Keep only if multiple dispersal strategies coexist, spatial autocorrelation scales differ, and each strategy can invade when rare in the other’s resident background.
morphology

One-bit developmental plasticity at each branch

Smallest ruleAllow a branch instruction to choose between two child subtrees using one local cue: neighbor density, contact, or local open-face count.
Natural pressureGenomes are rewarded for building context-appropriate bodies, not merely one static plan.
Expected visualThe same lineage forms compact interiors and exploratory margins; canopy-like and corridor-like morphs appear without separate species.
Why deeperPlastic genotype–phenotype maps can expose selectable variation and evolutionary innovation.[18] It directly addresses developmental censoring rather than adding a resource field.
Failure modeThe cue becomes a trivial stop-growth switch, reducing form rather than enriching it.
Keep / kill testClone the same genome into controlled density contexts. Keep if reaction norms evolve, improve lifetime seed output in both contexts, and increase realized-form diversity without merely lowering cell count.
temporal

Heritable phenology in a minimal season

Smallest ruleAdd a global periodic phase, but let genomes encode germination delay, growth onset and flowering window. Do not add rain or spatial resource maps.
Natural pressureEarly types capture space; late types avoid peak competition; pollen overlap or contact can couple timing to partners.
Expected visualSuccessional waves, pulses of different colors, dormancy and temporal mosaics visible in frame sequences.
Why deeperTime becomes an ecological niche and can support priority effects or coexistence. It is orthogonal to static geometry.
Failure modeOne phase locks to the external clock, or priority effects exclude rather than coexist.
Keep / kill testMeasure phase entropy and invasion-when-rare across seasons. Keep only if multiple timing strategies persist and swapping resident phase changes the invader’s advantage.
careful retry

One persistent environmental trace that organisms control

Smallest ruleWhen tissue dies, leave a single scalar trace that decays. A heritable sign determines whether the trace raises or lowers local germination cost; production itself costs energy.
Natural pressureOrganisms alter the future selective environment experienced by descendants and neighbors—ecological inheritance, not passive “soil quality.”
Expected visualSuccessional halos, inhibitory clearings, facilitative trails and lineage-specific landscape memory.
Why deeperNiche construction can create feedback and novel opportunities.[17] This revisits litter with a minimal bidirectional mechanism rather than a detailed soil simulator.
Failure modeThe trace becomes a static resource bonus, accumulates without bound, or selects universal non-production.
Keep / kill testCompare normal, shuffled-trace and no-trace controls. Keep only if trace–lineage associations persist across generations and causal trace removal changes succession.
form + tradeoff

Two visibly distinct tissue functions

Smallest ruleLet each stroke be photosynthetic tissue or structural/conductive tissue. Structural cells earn no light energy but reduce upkeep of supported distal tissue or allow one controlled crossing.
Natural pressureInvestment trades immediate income against reach, resilience and access to open space.
Expected visualTrunks and twigs, sparse long bridges, compact shrubs and visibly different construction strategies.
Why deeperFunctional differentiation expands the developmental vocabulary and may create preconditions for division of labor without adding another environmental field.
Failure modeOne tissue type dominates; the support rule becomes an arbitrary height bonus; crossings destroy legibility.
Keep / kill testUse a cost sweep and lesion tests. Keep only if mixed-tissue bodies outperform pure types in some contexts, multiple allocations coexist, and the tissue map remains readable at one pixel.
Recommended sequence: implement evolvable dispersal first because it is small and diagnostic; then partner-specific pollen/recombination or contact chemistry because those directly create reciprocal evolutionary dependence. Add plastic development only after lineage/event logging exists. Revisit litter or seasonality only in the minimal forms above, with explicit causal controls.
10 · Methods, audit trail and limits

How the conclusions were made

The experiment used three deterministic world seeds (1, 2, 3), a 440×735-cell world, one rendered pixel per cell, 40 identical red founders, default parameters, and exact captures after 10, 100, 1K, 10K, 100K and 1M simulation steps. The accelerated C++ runner was validated against the original JavaScript through 10K for seed 1: RNG state, all organism and seed records, and every RGB pixel matched at every checkpoint.

Derived measurements

  • Program morphology: recursive genome nodes, stroke length, terminal flowers, branch points, depth, direction use and exact form_code.
  • Realized morphology: occupied cells, flowers, bounding box, span, density and aspect class. Programmed cell count is total stroke length + 5 per flower instruction.
  • Color: circular mean and resultant, Shannon effective hues, exact circular pair gap min(|a−b|,256−|a−b|), nearest-neighbor gap, and pair gaps within radii 8–128.
  • Actual rarity advantage: the same bloom-weighted 16-cell blocks, 3×3 neighborhood, self-exclusion and circular mean used by the source; discount is half the normalized local gap.
  • Associations: Spearman rank correlations within living cross-sections. These are explicitly interpreted as survivorship descriptions, not causal lifetime fitness gradients.

Limits that constrain the language

  • Only three seeds and six cross-sections; no continuous trait trajectories.
  • No parent IDs, dead-organism archive, per-plant lifetime births or realized mating network.
  • Plants within a world are not independent statistical replicates; the world seed is the experimental unit.
  • Color receives direct designed negative frequency dependence. Morphology does not receive a global fitness score, but it does inherit the source’s specific metabolism and collision rules.
  • Exact-form richness is sensitive to high mutation and does not equal ecological or functional diversity.
  • Orientation uses realized bounding boxes and can be affected by crowding, world aspect ratio and founder history as well as genotype.
